review_notes: I read the whole file and looked for problems in its simp interface. The file has only one `@[simp]` lemma, `FormalMultilinearSeries.derivSeries_coeff_one`. It rewrites `p.derivSeries.coeff n 1` to `(n + 1) • p.coeff (n + 1)`. The right-hand side is smaller in terms of series structure, so I see no cycle. I found no competing simp rule for the left-hand side. I grepped Mathlib for `derivSeries_coeff_one`, `derivSeries_apply_diag` and `iteratedFDeriv_eq`, and found nothing that conflicts with it. The other identities are conditional and take explicit hypotheses or witnesses, for example `HasFPowerSeriesAt.fderiv_eq`, `ContinuousMultilinearMap.iteratedFDeriv_eq`, `derivSeries_apply_diag` and `changeOrigin_toFormalMultilinearSeries`. Adding `@[simp]` to them would be speculative, because their right-hand sides expand to more complex terms, and the rubric warns against that. The `fun_prop` coverage is uneven (`AnalyticAt.deriv` and `AnalyticAt.fderiv` have it, `AnalyticOnNhd.deriv` and `AnalyticOnNhd.differentiableOn` do not). That is not a simp rewrite problem, so I did not report it. The proofs call `simp`, `simpa` and `simp_rw` many times, and I looked for ones that depend on a fragile or overly expansive rule set. I found none with concrete evidence of a defect. I did not run Lean, so I cannot rule out simp-set interactions that only show up in practice.
